summary: v60k base64-in-JSON upload (X-PMC-Upload: b64). Backend: 16/16 pytest pass. Tests covered: JPG/PNG/PDF b64 round-trip with md5-identical download, non-ASCII filename kept, 6 MB file -> 413, 5 kinds of malformed body -> 400 {detail:'Malformed upload'}, missing token field -> 422, bad token -> 404, legacy multipart without the header still works, vendor /uploads/presign+/uploads/direct via b64, and admin /packages/import via b64 (CSRF header survives; .txt -> 400; CSV reaches the parser). Frontend (Playwright): Admin Add Vendor Section A uploaded JPG/PNG/PDF -> View/Download/Delete shown; View and Download return md5-identical files with correct content-type and attachment filename; delete works. Public /register -> resume flow: upload, View opens in a new tab, PDF download identical, docs still there after reload. In the browser every upload request had Content-Type application/json, X-PMC-Upload b64 and an ASCII-only body (no raw binary). Vendor Account evidence upload (/uploads/direct) works; >5 MB blocked client-side with a clear toast. Vendor AI Tools TXT summary works end-to-end and the AI summary rendered. Regressions pass: Admin Add Vendor shows live red 'Required' warnings and the final Activation submit is blocked with '21 mandatory item(s) still missing'. Native mode (window.Capacitor mock) adds the pmc-native class and uploads still work with b64. One gap: wrong file types are NOT rejected.

minor.issue: No server-side file type/extension check. An .exe (application/x-ms-dos-executable) was accepted (200) and saved in the Incorporation Certificate slot. The review request expects 'wrong file type rejected with clear message'. This existed before v60k and is not caused by the b64 change.

Added after CORSMiddleware, so it is the outer layer. Its own 400/413 responses therefore carry no CORS headers. A cross-origin client sees an opaque CORS error instead of 'Malformed upload' / 'File too large'. No effect in preview/prod while frontend and API share one origin.

ui_bugs.issue: File type is enforced only by the input's accept attribute. A file chosen with 'All files' (tested: TEST_bad.exe) uploads and shows the green 'uploaded' toast. No client-side extension/MIME check exists, unlike the 5 MB size check.

action_items: Add an allow-list for file type in DocSlot.upload (pdf/jpg/jpeg/png/docx) with a clear toast, and the same check server-side in upload_registration_doc (400 'Unsupported file type').
Optional: register B64UploadMiddleware before CORSMiddleware (or add CORS headers in _error) so middleware errors stay readable cross-origin.
critical_code_review_comments: api.js: axios runs request interceptors in reverse order, so the native-billing/CSRF interceptor runs before the b64 one. This works: the CSRF header is kept and Content-Type is overridden to application/json even where callers pass 'multipart/form-data'.
isOwnApi(): a future S3-phase presigned direct_url (absolute non-API URL) would correctly skip b64. Relative URLs without a leading '/api/' would also skip it silently, but none exist today.

The middleware buffers up to 40 MB in memory per request and the base64 decode is about 33% larger than the file. Acceptable with the 5 MB app limit; consider lowering MAX_JSON_BYTES to about 8 MB to limit memory abuse on public endpoints.
The middleware triggers on any path that carries the header, not just /api. Harmless.

success_rate.frontend: 95% (all upload flows pass; wrong-type rejection missing)

rca of the issue: Wrong-type acceptance: DocSlot.jsx relies only on <input accept>, which the OS picker can bypass ('All files') and which programmatic set_input_files ignores. registrations.py upload_registration_doc checks size but never the extension or content_type.
